A1.justification: Both PDFs describe D2E and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content can be matched across pagination changes, table renumbering, and appendix moves.

before.justification: v1 reports original recording and decoding benchmarks, Generalist-IDM evaluations, and VAPT results on LIBERO and CANVAS.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Meta-World, SO101 robot experiments, temporal-offset ablations, and training-loss analyses.

M1.justification: The OWA pipeline, InternVL3-based architecture, event tokenization, NEP/NEP-τ objectives, and VAPT training sequence remain unchanged. Specifying the existing temporal offset and context length adds documentation; the new downstream evaluations do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds Meta-World manipulation across four difficulty groups and physical SO101 pick-and-place evaluation with five cube positions. Existing desktop, LIBERO, and CANVAS coverage remains. Removing duplicate collection rows for Battlefield 6 and Ogu does not remove those games, which remain listed as OOD data.

E2.justification: Existing specialist-IDM, tooling, and LIBERO comparator sets are retained. The added benchmarks compare the same InternVL3 baseline and VAPT variants. SmolVLA supplies an evaluation protocol rather than an additional evaluated comparator in the new tables.

E3.justification: New protocols include Meta-World training for 50,000 steps and evaluation over 10 episodes per task, SO101 evaluation using 208 demonstrations and five initial positions, and a controlled 0–200 ms temporal-offset sweep. Existing LIBERO and CANVAS settings are retained; newly disclosed settings for existing training do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.1 tests the necessity and sensitivity of future context using five temporal offsets across six games. New Appendix E.1 and Figures 7–8 compare baseline and VAPT training losses on all four LIBERO suites and CANVAS, examining optimization behavior.

E5.justification: v2 adds repeated-trial information for the physical experiment, stating two trials per cube position. This does not reconcile with five positions and the separately stated 30 rollouts per model. Existing three-run benchmark and navigation descriptions remain unchanged, and no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Existing IDM, LIBERO, and CANVAS scores are retained. New Table 7 reports Meta-World averages of 19.9% for the baseline versus 25.0% and 24.8% for VAPT; Table 8 reports SO101 success of 70% versus 80% for both variants. Alternative-offset results and loss curves are added. The 100 ms per-game ablation rows reproduce earlier IDM scores with rescaling and rounding.

T1.justification: The NEP and NEP-τ objectives, token-decoding mathematics, and scale-ratio definitions remain equivalent in Equations 1–7. The new offset study is empirical and introduces no theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the three contributions and the headline claims of scalable desktop collection, generalist inverse dynamics, and desktop-to-robotics transfer. The reported 96.6% LIBERO and 83.3% CANVAS headline results remain unchanged; added experiments support the existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds transfer explanations based on action alignment, sequential decision-making, and dataset diversity, linking loss curves to better initialization while acknowledging incomplete mechanistic understanding. It also interprets the offset ablation as evidence for necessary future context and robustness above 100 ms. The unchanged simulation-only limitation now conflicts with the reported physical experiment.

D1.justification: Appendices B.4 and E newly disclose the 100 ms IDM offset and 8192-token training context. Appendix H.1 adds LeRobot v0.4.1, Meta-World training settings, and the SO101 camera arrangement, background, starting conditions, and collection details. The abstract replaces the project-site reference with a demo link; existing code and data release statements remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Meta-World citation to Yu et al. (2020) and explicitly connects the new downstream protocols to previously cited SmolVLA and LeRobot. Positioning relative to VPT, SIMA, and prior inverse-dynamics methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. Changes include local grammatical edits, revised downstream-results narration, new explanatory subsections, and an inserted ablation appendix that shifts downstream details, ethics, and limitations from G–I to H–J.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables for downstream results and temporal-offset ablations, plus two training-loss figures containing four LIBERO panels and a CANVAS plot. Figure 1 is refreshed, existing tables are reflowed or relocated, and duplicate collection rows are removed from the dataset table.

improvement.justification: The offset ablation and additional training details make the existing method better supported and easier to reproduce. Meta-World and SO101 provide useful additional transfer evidence. The benefit is tempered by the small physical comparison without uncertainty estimates, conflicting rollout counts in Appendix H.1, and the simulation-only limitation still retained in Appendix J.
